program_question: Do restricted correspondences between adaptive dynamical systems support quantitative stability laws and no-refit cross-class transport, or only local coordinate equivalences?

map.state: interior categorical probability vector p on the simplex
map.geometry: negative-entropy mirror geometry = categorical Fisher/Shahshahani geometry
map.clean_update: p_i' proportional to p_i exp(eta r_i)

scope: strictly interior clean states for KL/Fisher expressions
exact exponential categorical update or its stated continuous-time limit
float64 numerical comparisons at declared horizons and tolerances
edges.content: Within scope, the mapped clean probability trajectories must agree; ACL-002 additionally predicts the first-order L1 response to a frozen row-stochastic mutation perturbation.

stability.result: ACL-002 zero-fit analytic target gate passed. Posthoc residuals are predominantly negative, locally quadratic for T>1, and landscape dependent.

second_order_exploratory.result: The frozen posthoc earning rule passed with no target refit; all 12 regular T=20 targets gained 5% and 10% radius, but stress stability failed.

second_order_confirmation.law: delta_L1^(2)(epsilon,T) = ||epsilon s_T + (epsilon^2/2) u_T||_1 with O(epsilon^3) state remainder
second_order_confirmation.result: ACL-003 passed on 16 landscapes using entirely new state, reward, and mutation catalog values. At T=20, the maximum relative error per landscape over epsilon 0.001, 0.003, and 0.01 had median 0.148431% and Type-7 Q90 0.738712% with no fitting.

transport.quantity: median source-landscape alpha multiplying the analytic first-order coefficient
transport.result: Passed on 12 deterministic held-out target combinations with frozen alpha_source = 0.9951356698171323.
transport.scope_limit: within-family combinatorial held-out transport, not a different adaptive-system class

second_order_new_value.quantity: zero-fit analytic second-order truncated state response
second_order_new_value.result: Passed on 16 new-value categorical landscapes through epsilon 0.01.
second_order_new_value.scope_limit: stronger new-value transport within the categorical mutation class, not cross-class transport

failure_boundary.result: ACL-003 confirms second-order accuracy through epsilon 0.01 on new values. Stored non-gating stress rows show improvement on all 16 landscapes at epsilon 0.03 but only 13 at epsilon 0.1; T=20 second-order stress median is 3.652%, Q90 36.875%, and maximum 114.694%. The law is not uniformly stress-stable.
failure_boundary.unresolved: The exact analytic radius sufficient for uniform error control remains open; no cross-class stability transport has yet been tested.

edges.what_would_change_interpretation: Failure of an independently defined Gaussian bridge would confine the present predictive law to the categorical class; successful no-refit cross-class transport would support a restricted reusable correspondence theory.

map.candidate_update: separate mean and covariance rank-mu tangent blocks

scope: frozen lambda, mu, weights, parameterization, and learning rates
edges.content: The conditional expected finite-lambda rank-mu update should align with an independently constructed analytic Fisher-natural direction in each tangent block.

stability.law: finite-lambda expected rank-mu tangent from conditional binomial rank utility, Gaussian score, and inverse Fisher metric
stability.result: ACL-004 passed on 12 deterministic 3D landscapes. All converged at 4096 shadows; minimum mean-block Fisher cosine was 0.999952324 and minimum covariance-block cosine was 0.999552200 against a 0.99 gate.

transport.quantity: unchanged blockwise conditional-mean rule: disjoint-half Fisher cosine >= 0.98 followed by analytic Fisher cosine >= 0.99
transport.result: ACL-005 passed on 20 regular contextual-bandit context blocks; all stopped at 4096 and the minimum analytic Fisher cosine was 0.999841630.

failure_boundary.result: H2 concerns conditional expectations, not reliable individual steps. Stored H1 single-shadow median Fisher cosines span 0.953-0.957 for mean and 0.534-0.717 for covariance; covariance cosine is positive for 84.1%-87.9% of shadows. Lambda scaling was not studied.

edges.what_would_change_interpretation: A support-conditioned theorem must explain why the rule survives all regular control targets but fails despite convergence in rare-cell stress; failure of such a bound on new classes would narrow reuse to this Gaussian-control pair.

edges.content: The ACL-004 blockwise conditional-mean rule predicts held-out contextual-bandit policy-direction alignment without control-target refitting.

stability.law: conditional mean of undamped empirical-Fisher plug-in NPG compared blockwise with exact analytic NPG
stability.result: ACL-005 regular targets passed the transported 0.98/0.99 blockwise rule. Frozen rare-cell stress targets show that empirical-pseudoinverse bias can remain directionally wrong after disjoint-half convergence.

transport.quantity: ACL-004 unchanged blockwise 0.98 convergence and 0.99 analytic-alignment rule
transport.result: PASS on 10 regular landscapes and 20 context blocks; minimum cosine 0.999841630.

failure_boundary.result: All four non-gating rare-cell stress landscapes stopped at 4096, yet 5 of 8 context blocks were below 0.99 and the minimum was 0.055699373. Adequate cell coverage is a material scope condition; self-consistency alone is insufficient.

edges.what_would_change_interpretation: A theorem relating minimum joint-cell mass, sample count, empirical-Fisher rank, and angular bias would turn the observed regular/stress split into a predictive radius; counterexamples inside its proposed scope would refute that extension.

map.object: conditional mean of a finite-sample stochastic tangent compared with an independently analytic Fisher-natural tangent
map.stability_diagnostic: Fisher cosine between disjoint-half conditional-mean estimates

scope: ACL-004 pure diagonal Gaussian linear-rank source with lambda=32 and mu=16
ACL-005 two-context three-action categorical-policy target with N=128
regular target minimum expected joint-cell count at least 4
frozen replication schedule through 65536 and no target refit
edges.content: Once every target block reaches disjoint-half Fisher cosine 0.98, every regular target block should reach Fisher cosine 0.99 with its independent analytic direction.

stability.law: 0.98 disjoint-half block convergence predicts at least 0.99 analytic block alignment under the frozen regular-support scope
stability.result: All 20 regular target blocks passed; minimum analytic cosine 0.999841630.

transport.quantity: the complete dimensionless 0.98-to-0.99 blockwise diagnostic and unchanged replication schedule

failure_boundary.result: The law is not support-free: 5 of 8 rare-cell stress blocks failed the 0.99 target despite all stress landscapes satisfying the 0.98 stopping rule; minimum cosine 0.055699373.

edges.what_would_change_interpretation: A new adaptive class that fails the frozen rule despite adequate support would show pair-specific rather than reusable structure; a support-conditioned angular-bias theorem would strengthen the reusable-class interpretation.

edges.state_map: one interior three-action policy block with an explicit outside-context sampling category
edges.native_geometry: analytic categorical Fisher metric on the centered-logit tangent
edges.ideal_vector_field: d = F^+ g = r - mean(r) 1, independently defined from the analytic score gradient and Fisher metric
edges.realized_estimator: hat(d) = hat(F)^+ hat(g) from the same fixed-N multinomial count table, undamped with rcond=1e-12
scope_assumptions: fixed context probability and deterministic rewards
no damping, fitted baseline, clipping, state update, or target refit

transported_prediction.quantity: exact finite multinomial conditional mean, covariance-normalized Fisher error, angular envelope, and split-half/truth dissociation
transported_prediction.result: All exact-mean, dissociation, and stochastic contrast gates passed; maximum normalized direction score 1.707381, full-score median 0.609557, and Q90 1.272615.

failure_boundary.result: N p_min alone is insufficient when rare-context and rare-action support are factorized differently; support probabilities and Fisher spectrum without reward geometry are insufficient because additive reward shifts preserve d but generally change E[hat(d)].

edges.falsifying_observation: Any locked target whose sampled conditional mean violates its exact covariance-normalized five-score prediction or angular envelope; or any dissociation-stratum target that cannot become split-half aligned while remaining truth-misaligned at the fixed budget.
edges.structural_distance_note: ACL-006 remains inside the ACL-005 contextual-bandit empirical-Fisher estimator family and adds mechanism, not an independent adaptive class.

edges.state_map: adaptive tangent at a frozen state maps to terminal belief displacement from an initial belief
edges.native_geometry: source categorical Fisher tangent versus target centered Euclidean belief tangent
edges.ideal_vector_field: source analytic natural direction versus target exact true-model Bayes posterior displacement
edges.realized_estimator: source empirical-Fisher pseudoinverse shadow versus target finite labeled-particle bootstrap-filter displacement
scope_assumptions: independent estimator shadows around one frozen specification
finite second moment in the declared native metric
exact or independently computed estimator expectation and covariance
fixed schedule and no target refit

transported_prediction.quantity: ACL-006 unchanged standardized mean-error gates and split-consistency/truth-dissociation thresholds

edges.falsifying_observation: A preregistered target violates the unchanged ACL-006 normalized mean or dissociation gates despite exact target moments and an independently verified particle simulator.
edges.structural_distance_note: Different estimator family, native metric, objective semantics, temporal structure, data generation, and adaptation role; this is the first Phase-II candidate outside the Fisher-natural family.
